content.text:
**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

Section 17(b) already gives Sparkling a clean convenience exit — termination "at any time" on 90 days' written notice, with no early-termination fee or penalty. That sits at the top of our fallback notice range (60–90 days) and beats the fallback's tolerance for a fee of up to three months' fees.

On the vendor side, Garman has no convenience right at all: Section 17 allows Garman to terminate only for insolvency events or an uncured material default (17(c)), and the Section 10 maintenance term contains no at-will suspension or walk-away right. Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid, so there is no multi-year lock-in to escape.

Noted in the rationale but not redlined: 17(b) does not expressly require a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the refund at p0128 is limited to termination for Garman's default). That is a sub-element short of our preferred position, not a fallback failure, and exposure is limited by the annual maintenance term — so no redline was proposed.
